subject: Coordination: cross-border incident notification & evidence transfer
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medisyshealth.com>, Kyle Park <kyle.park@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coordination: cross-border incident notification & evidence transfer

Hi Alicia / Kyle —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I want to document the proposed notification and evidence-transfer approach so Legal and Ops can align before we finalize any contract language. Key points we discussed:

- Redwood will notify MediSys security within 24 hours of confirming a security incident that affects MediSys data; we will provide an initial impact summary (scope, user count range, affected regions).
- Evidence handover (logs / forensics artifacts) will be coordinated through a secure upload link. Redwood needs 5 business days to bundle and scrub logs for PII minimization before transfer, unless MediSys requests expedited access for active investigations.
- Cross-border constraint: If evidence requires export outside EU/UK regions, Redwood will flag the set and include the legal basis; transfers will use our standard SCCs or an approved data transfer mechanism.

Could you confirm the above is aligned with MediSys expectations and highlight any required SLAs or alternate timelines? I've looped in Laura for DPA wording and Monica for the operational handoff. I've attached a one-page evidence-handshake template that we can use as the transfer wrapper.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to provide redline language for the notification window and evidence transfer paragraph by Tue 20 Apr.
2) Monica to own the secure link and coordinate the transfer once we receive a formal request.
3) MediSys to confirm whether they require raw kernel-level logs (we'll need extra time/controls) or higher-level request traces.

Attachments: evidence_handshake_template.pdf (attachment stub)

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medisyshealth.com>

Subject: Re: Coordination: cross-border incident notification & evidence transfer

Sean —

Thanks for writing this up and for the template. High level: yes, that maps to our expectations. A few clarifications from our side so we can surface internal approvals:

- 24-hour initial notification window is acceptable for incidents where Redwood has high confidence; for incidents detected by MediSys, we expect reciprocal notification within 24 hours of our report.
- Evidence access: in most cases we only need request traces and session logs. We will call out any requests for lower-level artifacts in the formal request.
- Cross-border transfers: MediSys requires that any logs leaving the EU/UK are covered by SCCs or a previously approved DTA. Please attach your SCCs excerpt or transfer mechanism summary.

One ask: can Redwood commit to a maximum of 10 business days for producing full forensic packages if expedited handling is not approved? That gives our legal team clarity on timelines.

I'll also flag this to our Procurement team if there are any procurement-side timing dependencies.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Security & Privacy Operations
MediSys Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@medisyshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: cross-border incident notification & evidence transfer

Folks —

Thanks for the clear notes. Drafting a compact clause for the DPA and SOW that captures the notification and evidence transfer commitments. Key proposed language (high level):

- Notification: Redwood shall provide Customer with an initial written notice within 24 hours of becoming aware of an Incident that materially affects Customer Data, followed by a written update within 72 hours with the preliminary scope and mitigation steps.
- Evidence Transfer: Upon Customer's written request, Redwood will make reasonable efforts to provide access to relevant logs and artifacts necessary for Customer's investigation within 10 business days. If Customer requires expedited production (<=5 business days), Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts and may charge for accelerated processing.
- Cross-Border: Redwood will not export Customer Data outside the EEA/UK without lawful basis. Where transfer outside those regions is necessary for forensic analysis, Redwood will rely on SCCs or an equivalent mechanism and will notify Customer in the evidence request acknowledgement.

I'm attaching an SCC excerpt and a short flow diagram for the secure transfer (redwood-notify-flow.png). The attachments contain the mechanics IT will need: ticket workflow, encryption key exchange, and a checklist for PII minimization.

I'll circulate a redline for the DPA by EOD Tue 20 Apr. Sean / Monica: if you can confirm the ticketing intake phrase MediSys should use, we can route requests automatically into our incident queue.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Attachments: medisys-dpa-excerpt.pdf; redwood-notify-flow.png (attachment stubs)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medisyshealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coordination: cross-border incident notification & evidence transfer

Alicia / team —

Thanks. Operationally, here's the intake text you can paste into a request form or email which will route to our incident queue: 

"Please open a Redwood Evidence Request: Customer: MediSys Health; Case ID: <your internal ref>; Type: Forensic Logs / Session Traces; Priority: Normal / Expedited"

Once that ticket is created our playbook will:
1) Acknowledge within 4 business hours and provide an estimated delivery window (standard: 10 business days; expedited: 3-5 business days).
2) Prepare artifacts in a staging bucket with server-side encryption; we will provide a scoped manifest and a checksum.
3) Execute transfer via secure upload link; for cross-border transfers we will include transfer mechanism metadata and SCC reference.

I'll schedule a 30-min ops handoff with your Security Ops team on Wed 21 Apr to walk through the checklist and access controls. Proposed time: Wed 21 Apr, 10:00am PT. Let me know if that works.

Attachments referenced: evidence_handshake_template.pdf

Monica Patel
